question: Phulkari embroidery is related to the state of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Phulkari embroidery is a traditional folk art form that originated in the state of Punjab.
 
• It is characterized by intricate and colorful floral patterns, traditionally embroidered on shawls, dupattas, and other garments.
 
• The word 'Phulkari' translates to 'flower work', which reflects the floral designs that are predominant in this embroidery style.
 
• Phulkari is usually done on handwoven plain cloth using silk threads, and the designs are created using a variety of stitches, especially the darn stitch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Embroidery**

 
 
• Embroidery is the craft of decorating fabric or other materials using a needle to apply thread or yarn.
 
• Embroidery may also incorporate other materials such as pearls, beads, quills, and sequins.
 
• It is an ancient craft that has been practiced across different cultures and civilizations throughout history.
 
• Various techniques and stitches are used in embroidery, such as cross-stitch, chain stitch, satin stitch, and more.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Indian Textiles**
 
 
• India is known for its rich heritage of textiles, including various traditional forms of weaving, printing, and embroidery.
 
• Some of the well-known traditional textiles include Banarasi silk, Kanchipuram silk, Chanderi, Bandhani, and Ikat.
 
• Each region in India has its unique textile traditions that reflect the local culture, history, and resources.
 
• These textiles are often used in the making of sarees, salwar kameez, shawls, and other garments, as well as home decor items.
 
 
 
• **Phulkari Revival**
 
 
• In recent years, there has been a revival of Phulkari embroidery, with designers and artisans working to preserve and promote this traditional art form.
 
• Phulkari is now used in modern fashion, including contemporary clothing, accessories, and home decor items.
 
• Various initiatives and organizations are supporting artisans and providing platforms for showcasing Phulkari work.
 
• This revival not only preserves the cultural heritage but also provides livelihood opportunities for artisans in Punjab.
